items.title: Moonshot AI drops Kimi K3 open weights at 00:00 UTC July 27 (8pm ET July 26) — 2.8T-parameter MoE, 896 experts activating 16 per token (~50B live compute), 1M-token context, native video, Modified MIT license, ~594GB MXFP4 safetensors on Hugging Face; the largest open-weight model in AI history lands the same hour Washington is deciding whether to try to restrict it
items.summary: Moonshot AI released the full weights for Kimi K3 at 00:00 UTC on July 27, 2026 — roughly six hours before this snapshot went out — on Hugging Face under huggingface.co/moonshotai, under a Modified MIT license, exactly as promised on the July 16 API launch at the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai. K3 is a 2.8-trillion-parameter Stable-LatentMoE with 896 experts, of which the router activates only 16 per token, giving roughly 50 billion parameters of live compute per forward pass. Context window is 1 million tokens, natively multimodal including video, and the native release is quantization-aware trained in MXFP4 four-bit precision — the ~594GB safetensors download IS the reference release, not a lossy re-quant. Community BF16 and GGUF re-quants are already being uploaded within hours. Practical hardware floor to load the full model in MXFP4 is 8× H100 80GB (or 4× H200 141GB, or 2× Blackwell B300, or an equivalent MI400 configuration) — a single RTX 4090 or Mac Studio cannot run full K3 even at four-bit. The 7am EDT morning update: Together AI and Modal both confirmed day-0 hosted access within hours of the weights landing, Moonshot's own announcement racked up 7.2M+ views and nearly 6,000 likes overnight, and Moonshot paused new K3 subscriptions citing GPU capacity near limit — confirming the hosted-inference route is live now rather than 'within 24-48 hours.' The API-launch benchmark set that has now been open-weights-verifiable since 00:00 UTC: SWE-bench Verified 76.8%, FrontierSWE 81.2, Terminal-Bench 2.1 88.3, Program Bench 77.8, SWE Marathon 42.0, BrowseComp 91.2, GPQA Diamond 93.5%, MMMU-Pro 81.6. On the LMArena Frontend Code leaderboard K3 debuted at #1 with a 1,679 score in blind preference testing, first in six of seven frontend sub-domains, ahead of Claude Fable 5 (1,631) and GPT-5.6 Sol (1,618). On Artificial Analysis's aggregate Intelligence Index K3 scores 57 and sits fourth of 189 models. Pricing on Moonshot's hosted API is $0.60/M input and $2.40/M output.
items.why_it_matters: For Gabe: five reads. First, the specific 'largest open-weight model in AI history' read: 2.8 trillion total parameters, quantization-aware trained to MXFP4 native precision, released under a Modified MIT license on Hugging Face — this is the specific event where the frontier open-weights ceiling moved from ~1.6T (DeepSeek V4 Pro) to ~3T in a single drop, and the specific event where 'open weights are behind closed weights' stops being a defensible narrative on the aggregate Intelligence Index. K3 sitting fourth of 189 on Artificial Analysis puts it ahead of Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5 xhigh, and Claude Sonnet 5 — three closed-weights models most working developers were using as their default six weeks ago. Second, the specific 'you cannot run this locally, but hosted inference is live NOW' read: the practical hardware floor is 8× H100 80GB or equivalent, so a single RTX 4090 or Mac Studio cannot run it — but as of this morning (7am EDT), Together AI and Modal both confirmed day-0 hosted access, and OpenRouter had K3 available from API launch July 16. Moonshot paused new K3 subscriptions due to GPU capacity limits after 7.2M+ views, which is itself a signal of demand scale. The specific practical action item right now: try K3 via OpenRouter or Together AI, not by downloading weights. Third, the specific policy-timing read that makes this a Monday-July-27 story: the release lands into an active Trump-administration deliberation about restricting Chinese open-weight AI (executive order, Entity List, procurement rules, sanctions under the Bessent Treasury framework) — and the specific technical fact of the release is that restriction is now enforcement-impossible for anyone with a torrent client. Fourth, the specific 'what to actually do with K3' read: at SWE-bench Verified 76.8% and Terminal-Bench 2.1 88.3, K3 is competitive with Claude Sonnet 5 and GPT-5.5 for autonomous-agent workflows at roughly one-fifth the API cost. Fifth, the specific cascade-effect read: within 24-48 hours, expect community BF16 and GGUF re-quants, additional hosted-inference providers, and an OpenRouter market-share spike.

items.title: Nvidia open-weights letter still at 50 signatories Monday morning July 27 with Anthropic, Amazon, and xAI still off the list; Anthropic's silence now runs directly into the Kimi K3 weight-drop overnight, and multiple outlets frame Anthropic as the sole US frontier lab whose commercial model requires the White House to restrict what Moonshot has just made freely downloadable — 72-hour Anthropic response window opens today
items.summary: The Nvidia-hosted 'Open Weights and American AI Leadership' letter, first published Thursday July 24 with 25 signatories and doubled to 50 by Sunday July 26 (with OpenAI and Google flipping over the weekend), stayed at 50 through Monday morning July 27, 2026 with Anthropic, Amazon, and xAI still absent — the same three organizations flagged as absentees on Sunday afternoon. The Monday-morning enrichment update: no new signatories, no removals, no Anthropic response of any kind. Digitimes, Startup Fortune, Lanka Biznews, Corenexis, and Digital Applied have consolidated around a specific Monday-morning framing that treats the Kimi K3 weight release six hours ago as the specific stress-test event for Anthropic's closed-weights position — the letter argues open weights strengthen safety, cybersecurity, and sovereignty; the K3 release ~594GB safetensors under Modified MIT license actually delivers that at frontier scale; Anthropic's position that open source is 'a red herring' (Dario Amodei) now has to survive a working counter-example that ranks fourth of 189 on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index. Digitimes specifically frames the letter as 'Nvidia backs open-weight AI as OpenAI, Anthropic lobby for tighter controls' — the specific claim being that Anthropic and (previously) OpenAI have been actively lobbying the Trump administration for the Kimi K3 restriction package, which is a more aggressive positioning than 'chose not to sign a pro-open-weights letter.' The specific Monday-morning structural read: Anthropic is now the only US frontier lab whose stated policy position (weights once released cannot be recalled or made safe) is publicly at odds with the working evidence on Hugging Face (K3 weights are on Hugging Face, and both the US developer stack via OpenRouter and the US government via any imaginable executive order will now have to live with that fact). Coalition membership as of Monday morning: AI21, AMD, American Innovators Network, AMP, Andreessen Horowitz, Arcee AI, Arena, Baseten, Black Forest Labs, Block, Box, Cisco, Cloudflare, Cohere, CrowdStrike, Dell, DoorDash, Emergence Capital, Fireworks AI, Genspark, GitHub, Google, Hugging Face, IBM, Inferact, Interconnects AI, The Linux Foundation, Mariana Minerals, Meta, Microsoft, Mistral, Morph, Mozilla, Nebius, Nous Research, NVIDIA, Ollama, OpenAI, OpenClaw, Palantir, Palo Alto Networks, Periodic Labs, Perplexity, Prime Intellect, Reflection, Replit, ServiceNow, Telnyx, Trajectory, Y Combinator.
items.why_it_matters: For Gabe: three reads that firmed up overnight. First, the specific 'Anthropic-as-lone-holdout' read is now a real story rather than a weekend framing: the K3 weights actually landed at 00:00 UTC, the Nvidia letter still has 50 signatories with the same three absentees (Anthropic, Amazon, xAI), and Anthropic has not issued any public statement on the letter, the K3 release, or the Trump-administration restriction deliberations. The specific practical implication: whatever Anthropic communications team decides to do this week is now a first-order signal — silence continues to read as 'we are actively lobbying against open weights and prefer to do it privately,' any public statement will be scrutinized for specific alignment with the Trump-restriction package or specific distance from it. The specific 72-hour window that opens today is the specific window in which the story either becomes 'Anthropic breaks with the open-weights consensus explicitly' or 'Anthropic maintains awkward silence through a policy inflection.' Second, the specific Digitimes-and-Startup-Fortune escalation to 'Anthropic is actively lobbying for restrictions' read: this is now the specific interpretation multiple outlets are running rather than a fringe framing. Anthropic's July 22 Axios-reported alignment with OpenAI on 'open-weight AI risks' is now the specific evidence being cited to argue that Anthropic's absence from the Huang letter is not passive neutrality — it is active opposition. That's the specific reputational-risk read worth carrying for any developer choosing Claude for professional work: the model provider you use has a specific public-policy position that most of the rest of the US technology industry now opposes. Third, the specific policy-mechanics read for the rest of the week: the letter's 50-signatory coalition, the K3 weights being on Hugging Face, and the OpenRouter 46.4%-and-climbing market-share number (see sibling item) are now all specific ammunition in the specific Washington deliberation about restricting Chinese open-weight AI. The specific concrete signal to watch through Friday: (a) whether Anthropic issues any statement, (b) whether any additional US labs sign the letter, (c) whether the White House makes a specific K3 policy announcement.

items.summary: Updated OpenRouter usage figures covered across Yahoo Finance, eWeek, and Dataconomy over the weekend of July 25-26 and refreshed Monday morning July 27 show Chinese AI models continuing to expand their share of routed tokens on OpenRouter — the popular API-aggregation platform US developers use to plug into multiple AI models through a single API. The weekend-of-July-25-26 snapshot captured in yesterday's pm digest showed Chinese models at 46.4% of platform-wide tokens vs 35.7% for US models. Updated Monday-morning figures (Dataconomy Feb 2026 baseline of 61%, eWeek 60% US-business-only slice, Yahoo Finance 63% during first week of July for US-enterprise slice) show that the 46.4% platform-wide number is now specifically the LOWER-BOUND estimate — the US-enterprise-and-US-business slices where OpenRouter usage is heaviest sit in the 58-to-63% range. Chinese models still hold eight of the top ten most-used models on OpenRouter with only Anthropic's Claude family (aggregate 13.3% token share) remaining as a US-lab representative in the top ten. OpenAI and Google both remain out of the top ten entirely. The specific Kimi-K3 update overnight: with K3 weights now live on Hugging Face and Together AI and Modal already confirmed for day-0 hosted access, the OpenRouter Chinese-model share is expected to climb further this week as K3 debuts as the new default frontier-tier low-cost route.
items.why_it_matters: For Gabe: three reads that firmed up overnight. First, the specific 'this is not a rounding error and it is accelerating' read: Chinese AI models are now 46.4%-to-63% of OpenRouter routed tokens depending on which slice you look at, and Kimi K3 open weights landing at 00:00 UTC July 27 (six hours before this snapshot) is the specific event that will push the number higher this week. Second, the specific 'K3 changes the shape of the story from price-only to price-AND-quality' read: post-K3-open-weights, the honest narrative is 'a Chinese open-weight model at $0.30-0.50/M input debuts at #1 on LMArena Frontend Code and fourth of 189 on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index — ahead of Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5 xhigh, and Sonnet 5 — at ~10% of Claude Opus 5's price.' Third, the specific Washington-policy read: the 46.4-to-63% number is the specific concrete data point Washington is citing in its Kimi K3 executive-order deliberations, and the technical fact that both K3 weights (~594GB on Hugging Face) and DeepSeek V4/V4 Pro weights cannot be recalled means the specific restriction package options narrow to Entity-List addition of Moonshot, federal-procurement rules, security-threat advisories, or sanctions under the Bessent Treasury framework — none of which prevent a US developer with an OpenRouter API key from accessing K3.

items.title: Nvidia in talks to backstop $250B for OpenAI's lease of SoftBank's 10GW Ohio campus, plus $350B more in chip financing — a $500B+ deal that would make Nvidia the financial architect of AI infrastructure and give OpenAI its first owned compute, away from Microsoft
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported Sunday July 26 that Nvidia is in talks to provide a roughly $250 billion financial guarantee backing OpenAI's lease of SoftBank's SB Energy PORTS Technology Campus in Piketon, Ohio — a planned 10-gigawatt AI data center complex that would be the largest single compute campus ever built. The guarantee is not equity or a direct investment: it's a contractual backstop that would cover OpenAI's lease payments if OpenAI defaults, which matters because OpenAI lacks an investment-grade credit rating needed to finance a project of this scale on its own. Separately, Nvidia is also in talks to provide financing for OpenAI's chip purchases that could total an additional $350 billion, bringing the potential full scope of Nvidia's financial exposure to OpenAI's build-out to roughly $600 billion across both arrangements. The total cost of the campus including chips is estimated at $500 billion or more. First phase: 800 megawatts of capacity targeted for 2028. The deal, if completed, would rank among the largest financing arrangements in corporate history. Nothing is signed; the Wall Street Journal noted the terms are still moving and the talks could fall apart. Bloomberg confirmed the reporting independently. Context: the Piketon, Ohio site is a federally-owned former uranium enrichment facility (the Portsmouth Gaseous Diffusion Plant), and SoftBank's SB Energy subsidiary is developing it as part of SoftBank's announced US AI investment commitments following meetings with President Trump.
items.why_it_matters: For Gabe: three reads. First, the specific 'Nvidia becomes the financial architect of AI infrastructure' read: this isn't Nvidia investing in OpenAI's equity or just selling chips in a purchase agreement. A financial guarantee is a legally-binding pledge to cover another party's payment obligations if they default — Nvidia is putting its own balance sheet behind OpenAI's ability to lease a $500B campus. The specific incentive structure: Nvidia guarantees the lease, and in exchange it locks in OpenAI as a multi-decade chip customer, with another $350B in chip financing under separate discussion. For any developer, the concrete implication is that Nvidia's commercial interests are now structurally tied to OpenAI's scale of compute — which is also Nvidia's strongest incentive to keep OpenAI's prices competitive and its capacity growing. Second, the specific 'OpenAI exits the Microsoft orbit' read: the deal is explicitly framed as OpenAI's first step toward controlling its own infrastructure rather than renting from Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services, and Oracle Cloud. For a Python developer using OpenAI's API, the specific thing that changes if this campus is built: OpenAI's service capacity, pricing decisions, and availability windows will stop being limited by Microsoft Azure allocation agreements. The specific latency implication: Microsoft's Azure has been the primary constraint on OpenAI's capacity expansion since 2022; owning 10GW of compute by the early 2030s makes OpenAI's infrastructure roughly comparable to Microsoft's entire AI infrastructure today. The caveat: the first phase only delivers 800MW by 2028, so full 10GW is a 5-to-10-year build story. Third, the specific 'this is how much AI infrastructure actually costs' framing: $500B+ for a single campus is roughly 14% of Nvidia's entire market cap as of early 2026 — spent by one customer. The specific relevance for a developer wondering why API prices haven't fallen faster: compute at the frontier is the primary cost constraint, and a single campus at this scale represents the kind of investment that makes frontier compute effectively a national-infrastructure project rather than a standard tech capex item.
items.why_it_matters_brief: Nvidia would backstop $250B for OpenAI to lease SoftBank's 10GW Ohio campus — cementing Nvidia as financial architect of AI infrastructure and giving OpenAI its first owned compute outside Microsoft's orbit.
